SMTO-HTTP-0015 — The Gateway refused to send a web request

GUID: 1213e305-9218-4eab-81e9-e661ce51dcc8
Slug: http-gateway-request-rejected
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to reach other computers and services) turned down SMTO's web request before contacting the service. The service wasn't reached, so nothing changed there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways. If the selected Gateway shows Update available, expand it and select its Update button once its running tasks are finished. An older Gateway may not understand SMTO's web requests; updating it stops its running tasks, so wait for them first.
  2. After updating, ask SMTO in the conversation to send the same web request again. The service was never contacted, so sending the request again won't repeat any change.
  3. If the Gateway is already up to date, ask SMTO to try a simpler form of the request, such as one address and a standard method like GET or POST. The Gateway refuses requests whose details it can't accept, so resending the identical request won't help.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the web service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages SMTO; the Gateway's own log shows why it refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway's /http/request route returned 400, 404, 405, 422 or 501 to the Server's native HTTP dispatch, so the request was rejected before reaching the target service.

What this means

  • The Gateway HTTP route returned 400, 404, 405, 422 or 501 to the controller's native HTTP dispatch. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway HTTP route returned 400, 404, 405, 422 or 501 to the controller's native HTTP dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway route/status and request contract; this is distinct from a response by the destination API.

How to fix it

  • GatewayClient.http_request maps a 400, 404, 405, 422 or 501 from the Gateway's /http/request route (direct or outbound session) to this error before target execution. Check the Gateway log for the rejection reason; update the Gateway if it lacks or mismatches the native HTTP route (404/405/501), or correct the rejected request fields (400/422).
  • Inspect the Gateway rejection fields and submit a supported HTTP request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected Gateway accepts the supported native HTTP request protocol.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
